newsitem.title: CHINA: China share indices end mostly up, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: China share indices end mostly up, mood cautious.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended mostly up on Thursday, except the Shanghai B index, which edged down with most capital attracted by surging H shares and waiting for new B share issues, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.518 points or 0.67 percent to 76.448 on volume of 10.223 million shares worth $4.392 million.

The Shenzhen index gained 0.91 points or 0.68 percent to 133.64 points after hitting an intraday low of 132.22 on turnover of HK$46 million and its A index rose 5.54 points or 1.35 percent to 415.13 on turnover of 6.8 billion yuan.

The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index of H shares outperformed the blue-chip Hang Seng index, trading up 53.84 points or 4.78 percent to 1,179.12 points in the early afternoon on Thursday on restructuring rumours.
Brokers said the surging H shares sucked a lot of foreign money out of Shanghai B shares and at least two new B share issues this month had also drawn some capital.
"The B share market is quiet because Hong Kong has surged," said an analyst at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "A lot of foreign investors are looking at the H share market."
H shares are shares of Chinese companies listed in the former British colony of Hong Kong, which became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1.

Sentiment on the Shanghai B share market was also hurt by an editorial in Thursday's Financial News which said China's stock markets had been brought under control by natural market forces, rather than heavy-handed government intervention.
"The editorial showed signs that the government would like the market to linger in a narrow range rather than fluctuate," one local analyst said.
Analysts in Shenzhen said investors there were paying more attention to first-half earnings during the 1997 interim corporate reporting season which would end on August 30, analysts said.

Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Co Ltd rose HK$0.12 to HK$3.70 on volume of 1.37 million shares, making it the second most actively traded Shenzhen stock. Investors expected robust interim profits from the company, brokers said.

Newcomer Beijing Yanjing Brewery Co Ltd, which listed 72 million A shares on Wednesday, surged 1.52 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up at 16.72 yuan on Thursday. Volume reached 19 million shares, making it the most actively traded A share.
Shanghai Material Trading Co was the biggest loser on the Shanghai B share market on one speculative selling, tumbling $0.012 or 7.79 percent to $0.142 on volume of 13,000 shares.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the most actively traded on institutional profit-taking, falling $0.028 or 3.14 percent to $0.862 on volume of 804,800 shares.

Shanghai's A share index edged up 7.103 points 0.57 percent to 1,252.014 points on volume of 439.1 million shares worth 5.5 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index gained 29.793 points or 0.77 percent to to 3,874.469 points.
